limitations: All 138 parent queries plus eighteen frozen unique random/hidden-binary/deletion/parity inputs and four exact normalized repeats. Labels never guide acquisition; synthetic families recur and this is not external generalization.

Base executes the unchanged current implementation: shared pair prefixes, one batch of 256 attempts and 32 clauses. Larger uses the same implementation with 512/64. Feedback uses at most two 256/32 batches, the second against the checked final residual of an unresolved depth-zero terminal. Each changed CNF gets a fresh occurrence index and pair ranking.

Larger and feedback share maximum pair/learned-clause allowances, not equal actual work. With depth two there are at most four original leaves: 2048 candidate pairs and 256 retained binary clauses per root. Feedback can run eight terminal preparations versus four for larger; all costs are charged. Pair checking verifies consequences and retained-clause caps; it does not certify the number of unsuccessful searches, exhaustion or deterministic selection.

Exact intermediate sources and all incoming model maps are checked; rounds form an ordered list of length at most two, with no continuation after a verdict and no empty retained batch. Certificates do not prove polynomial unrestricted complexity or a new tractable family.

Four cyclic process orders start empty with the same fallback. Complete time includes input, discovery with internal verification, explicit checking, persistence, warm/cold replay and compression. Startup, labels, diagnostics, lineage audit and historical acquisition are extra. Two native readers audit fallback archives; JSON replay has two passes of one checker.
Unknown leaves including those under SAT parents remain represented. No production default changes; regressions and unresolved cases are retained.
